incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-05-21-512
executiveSummary: On 21-May-2025, a major e-commerce client reported a high volume of HTTP 499 (Client Closed Request) errors on our Create Transaction API. Our investigation confirmed that PayU's systems were operating within normal latency SLOs. The errors were traced back to the client's load balancer having a fixed timeout of 3 seconds, which was insufficient during peak processing times when third-party bank responses occasionally exceeded this threshold.
impact: Approximately 152 payment initiation requests failed. No PayU infrastructure was impacted.
impactedTransactions: 152 failed requests for the 'Create Transaction' endpoint.
psdiiReportable: False. The issue was client-side.
impactedApplication: Client's E-commerce Backend
accountableParty: Client-side Integration due to a 3-second timeout.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: Client application prematurely closed HTTP connections due to a 3-second load balancer timeout.
mitigation: Advised client to increase timeout to 10 seconds and implement exponential backoff.
timeline: 14:30 - Alert triggered. 14:32 - Client raised ticket. 14:35 - Investigation started. 15:00 - Cause identified. 15:15 - Findings communicated.
problemRecords: False. External issue resolved via guidance.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-06-11-598
executiveSummary: On 11-Jun-2025, a travel client reported refund automation failures due to HTTP 499 errors. The cause was a new 2-second timeout in their script, which was insufficient.
impact: 48 refund requests failed, causing manual overhead for the client. PayU's service was not impacted.
impactedTransactions: 48 failed requests for the 'Process Refund' endpoint.
psdiiReportable: False. Client-side configuration error.
impactedApplication: Client's Refund Automation Service
accountableParty: Client-side Integration due to an aggressive 2-second timeout.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: Client's refund script terminated the connection due to a 2-second timeout, below the P99 latency.
mitigation: Advised client to increase timeout to 8 seconds and implement a status check mechanism.
timeline: 11:05 - Client reported issue. 11:10 - Escalated to L2. 11:35 - Log analysis began. 11:50 - Identified 499 pattern. 12:05 - Report sent to client.
problemRecords: False. Client-side issue resolved via guidance.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-07-19-640
executiveSummary: On 19-Jul-2025, the same e-commerce client from a previous incident again reported HTTP 499 errors. The issue was a recurrence of a premature timeout setting that had been reverted during a deployment.
impact: 95 transaction requests failed, repeating impact on sales. No impact on PayU systems.
impactedTransactions: 95 'Create Transaction' API calls were impacted.
psdiiReportable: False. Recurring client-side configuration issue.
impactedApplication: Client's E-commerce Backend
accountableParty: Client-side Integration, due to failure to permanently apply the recommended timeout.
repeatIncident: True. Repeat of incident PAYU-INC-2025-05-21-512.
rootCause: Client-side timeout of 3 seconds was re-introduced. Lack of configuration management on the client side.
mitigation: Strongly reiterated the 10-second timeout, advised adding it to IaC, and scheduled a follow-up call.
timeline: 18:00 - Automated monitor flagged recurrence. 18:02 - Proactively created incident. 18:10 - Confirmed cause. 18:15 - Contacted client. 18:45 - Client confirmed fix.
problemRecords: False. External fault, but a problem record was opened on the client's side.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2024-11-10-119

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-04-01-404
executiveSummary: On 01-Apr-2025, a subset of transactions experienced elevated latencies, peaking at 12 seconds, due to a degraded database read replica caused by an unoptimized internal analytics query.
impact: ~2,500 transactions were delayed. 3 clients reported timeouts. Internal dashboards were slow.
impactedTransactions: 2,500 transactions were delayed.
psdiiReportable: True. Degradation of a core payment service.
impactedApplication: PayU Core Payment Processing
accountableParty: PayU Internal Analytics Platform.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: A new, un-tested analytics query consumed excessive I/O on a production read replica.
mitigation: The SRE team terminated the query, and the analytics job was disabled. Performance returned to normal.
clientRecommendations: A post-mortem was shared with impacted clients.
timeline: 11:15 - Latency alerts triggered. 11:20 - SRE investigation started. 11:30 - High I/O wait found on DB. 11:42 - Offending query terminated. 11:45 - System normal.
problemRecords: True. PRB-2025-088 created to optimize the query and review policies.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2024-12-25-180
executiveSummary: On 25-Dec-2024, all transactions via 'MegaBank India' failed for 45 minutes due to an outage at the bank's end. PayU systems were healthy and auto-rerouted traffic where possible.
impact: ~800 transactions failed. Overall success rate dropped by 3%. Most traffic was successfully re-routed.
impactedTransactions: 800 failures isolated to the MegaBank network.
psdiiReportable: False. Outage was caused by an external third party.
impactedApplication: PayU Bank Acquirer Integration
accountableParty: MegaBank India (Third Party).
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: Total network outage at third-party partner MegaBank India.
mitigation: Intelligent routing automatically de-prioritized MegaBank. The partner was automatically re-enabled once healthy.
clientRecommendations: No action required from clients.
timeline: 08:00 - Partner failure alerts fired. 08:02 - Automated routing disabled partner. 08:10 - Declared external incident. 08:40 - MegaBank acknowledged issue. 08:45 - Partner API back online and auto-re-enabled.
problemRecords: False. External dependency issue.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-03-18-350
executiveSummary: On 18-Mar-2025, a deployment misconfiguration caused the API Gateway to apply a low rate-limit policy, causing HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) errors for high-volume merchants.
impact: 12 enterprise clients were impacted. Over 4,000 legitimate requests were rejected.
impactedTransactions: 4,000 legitimate API calls were incorrectly throttled.
psdiiReportable: True. A significant portion of traffic was rejected by an internal failure.
impactedApplication: PayU API Gateway
accountableParty: PayU DevOps Team due to a faulty deployment script.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: A CI/CD script bug applied a default low rate-limit policy (100 RPM) instead of the intended 10,000 RPM policy.
mitigation: The faulty deployment was immediately rolled back, restoring service within 5 minutes.
clientRecommendations: An apology and RCA were shared with impacted clients.
timeline: 15:00 - Deployment completed. 15:02 - HTTP 429 alerts triggered. 15:03 - Clients reported errors. 15:05 - Rollback initiated. 15:10 - Rollback completed, issue resolved.
problemRecords: True. PRB-2025-055 created to fix the CI/CD script.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2025-07-02-610
executiveSummary: On 02-Jul-2025, a large-scale carding attack was detected. The WAF correctly blocked the attack but inadvertently impacted three legitimate clients using a shared proxy IP, causing them to see HTTP 403 errors.
impact: Three clients experienced intermittent HTTP 403 errors. 50-100 legitimate transactions were blocked. No fraudulent transactions were processed.
impactedTransactions: Up to 100 legitimate transactions blocked as collateral damage.
psdiiReportable: False. System behaved as designed to stop a threat.
impactedApplication: PayU Security Infrastructure (WAF)
accountableParty: External Attackers.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: A carding attack forced automated IP blocking. Legitimate clients were on a shared IP that was part of the blocked range.
mitigation: Client IPs were added to an allow-list, and the blocking rule was refined.
clientRecommendations: Recommended clients use a dedicated static IP for API traffic.
timeline: 02:00 - Carding attack detected. 02:05 - WAF enabled blocking. 02:30 - Client reported 403 errors. 02:45 - SOC investigated and found false positive. 03:45 - Client IP allow-listed.
problemRecords: True. PRB-2025-130 created to improve client identification beyond IP addresses.

incidentId: PAYU-INC-2024-10-05-099
executiveSummary: On 05-Oct-2024, the merchant settlement report generation service failed to run because an internal service account password had expired and was not rotated.
impact: Daily settlement reports for all merchants were not generated. Increased support tickets. No impact on payment processing.
impactedTransactions: 0. Report generation was impacted, not transactions.
psdiiReportable: False. Ancillary, non-payment service was affected.
impactedApplication: PayU Merchant Reporting Service
accountableParty: PayU Platform Operations due to operational oversight.
repeatIncident: False.
rootCause: The password for the 'svc_reportgen' service account expired and was not in the automated rotation system.
mitigation: The password was manually reset, and the report job was re-triggered.
clientRecommendations: A notification was sent to merchants about the delay.
timeline: 09:00 - Missing reports confirmed. 09:15 - Investigation started. 09:45 - Found 'Authentication Failed' errors in logs. 10:00 - Identified expired password. 10:30 - Password rotated and job re-run.
problemRecords: True. PRB-2024-211 created to onboard all service accounts to the credential management platform.
